key_insight: Physics-informed machine learning can accurately predict cRPA-derived Hubbard parameters (U_eff,V,J) for transition-metal oxides while revealing the physical descriptors that control electron correlation.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, scalable input generation for DFT+U, DFT+DMFT, and related beyond-DFT workflows, reducing reliance on costly first-principles cRPA calculations.
method: Ensemble-learning models trained on cRPA data for transition-metal oxides
Regression-based brute-force search to derive explicit analytical expressions
Physically motivated features: TM-d bandwidth, TM-d/O-p band-center separation, and structural/atomic descriptors
evidence_signal: The reported ensemble models achieved RMSEs of 0.148 eV for U_eff, 0.062 eV for V, and 0.007 eV for J on the evaluated dataset.
watch_item: Model transferability may be limited outside transition-metal oxides or when electronic structure lies far from the training distribution.
paper_title: Physics-informed Machine Learning Prediction of Hubbard Interaction Parameters
